newsitem.title: ITALY: NGOs seek sharing of wealth to fight hunger.
newsitem.headline: NGOs seek sharing of wealth to fight hunger.

text.p: Non-governmental organisations on Tuesday debated a draft statement to be presented to this week's World Food Summit which slams big-business farming and calls on rich countries to share their wealth to stamp out hunger.

Delegates to the NGO Forum are seeking to formulate a strongly worded statement to counter what many have described as "watered-down" positions to be adopted at the official five-day summit, which begins on Wednesday.

Their proposed statement, which delegates will discuss and revise before its presentation to the summit later this week, calls for "a reorientation of all aspects of food and agriculture in favour of the small-scale producer..."

"We propose a model of economic decentralisation that challenges the current model, which has produced a concentration of wealth and power that now threatens global food security, cultural diversity and the very ecosystems that sustain life on this planet."
The document is particularly harsh towards commercial agriculture and trade liberalisation, saying: "The ongoing globalisation of agriculture production and consumption has increased world poverty".

"Rich countries subsidise their exports, creating volatility in the world market, which bankrupts small producers and destroys rural economies," it says. "Furthermore, constant dumping and even some food aid programmes make people in Third World countries dependent on food they are unable to produce."
Organisers say the NGO Forum has brought together representatives of some 1,000 organisations covering a wide range of causes.
Among those present are charities such as Bread for the World, natural family planning advocates, an Amazon economic cooperation organisation and a group of Egyptian street vendors.

They are meeting in a cavernous former railway station, which has the feel of an airplane hangar, a short distance from the Rome headquarters of the U.N. Food and Agriculture Organisation where the World Food Summit will take place.

A main point of the NGO document is a demand for a sharing of wealth, through more investment by developed countries and the forgiving of Third World debt or its conversion into food security programmes.

"The adoption of International Monetary Fund and World Bank structural adjustment programmes and the debt obligations of Third World countries force these countries to shift their focus from establishing national food security to paying off the enormous debt, to the detriment of small farmers and consumers in general," the NGO document says.
